## Natural history notes

A small gall wasp characterized less by the adult insect, which is tiny and dark, and more by the rounded woody galls it produces on live oak. In Florida, it is associated with live oaks in hammocks, parks, yards, roadsides, and other wooded or landscaped areas where suitable host trees occur. The larvae develop inside protective oak galls, feeding within the plant tissue, while the adults are short-lived and often overlooked; the galls may provide shelter or food for other small insects after the wasp emerges.
